packages.objective: Implement and document the anonymous desktop bootstrap v1 handshake without adding any future desktop capability or database behavior.
deliverables: Exact anonymous GET response matching desktop-bootstrap@v1.
Closed JSON Schema, recognized fixture and integration handoff documentation.
Deterministic route tests for exact response, unsupported method, replay, version pinning, concurrency and recovery.
nonGoals: No device authorization, account, balance, usage, pricing projection, tool-key, payment, database, migration, deployment or client-source change.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No schema, database or customer-data migration belongs to this package.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert only the owned route, handler, tests and documentation; no data recovery is required.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Add one versioned anonymous route without changing existing routes. Keep v1 closed and capability flags false.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: desktop-bootstrap@v1 with minimum client version 0.1.0 only.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Removal or semantic expansion requires a superseding decision, versioned contract and new frozen release unit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Anonymous GET returns the exact closed v1 JSON response and content type.
An unsupported method does not expose the handshake or mutate state.
Repeated reads return an equivalent declaration with every capability false.
Schema version, contract ID and minimum client version remain pinned to the closed v1 contract.
Concurrent anonymous reads remain equivalent and side-effect free.
A valid GET succeeds after an unsupported method without manual recovery or state repair.

stopConditions: The client schema differs from the frozen observed contract.
Any capability would need to become true.
Any change requires authentication, database, migration, payment, deployment or a path outside allowedPaths.

packages.objective: Implement the versioned desktop v2 bootstrap, Redis-only browser-approved device authorization, JSON desktop refresh/logout adapters, and the authenticated browser approval surface while mapping all read and tool-key capabilities to existing NewAPI APIs.
deliverables: Immutable v1 plus a closed v2 bootstrap with exact existing route mappings and fixed comparison rate 6.75.
Five-minute Redis-only device authorization with explicit live-browser approval, bounded polling and single session issuance.
Desktop JSON refresh and current-session revocation backed by existing user_sessions.
Authenticated browser approval page that displays the user code and client name and requires explicit approve or deny.
Contract, route, concurrency, replay, expiry, refresh, revocation and browser behavior tests.
nonGoals: No database schema, migration, duplicate account table, duplicate billing data, payment processing, deployment, Nginx or production configuration change.
No new tool-key table or desktop-specific read projections; v2 advertises the existing authenticated owners.
No client repository change in this server release unit.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No schema or customer-data migration. Pending authorization exists only in Redis for five minutes; successful sessions use the existing user_sessions table.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Remove v2 routes and approval UI. Existing v1 and user_sessions remain valid; pending Redis keys expire naturally.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Keep desktop bootstrap v1 byte-for-byte compatible and add an independent v2 contract with minimum desktop version 0.2.0.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: desktop-bootstrap@v1 remains recognition-only; desktop integration v2 adds device authorization and session adapters while reusing existing authenticated APIs.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: V1 removal or v2 semantic change requires a successor version and frozen release unit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: V1 stays exact while v2 advertises only implemented existing routes, fixed 6.75 and live Redis availability.
A browser-approved unexpired device code issues one dedicated desktop user_session and no new table.
Missing Redis, malformed codes, pending, slow-down, denied and expired states never issue credentials.
Concurrent exchange of one approved code creates at most one session and later replay is rejected.
Desktop refresh rotates the secret and logout revokes only the current session while a failed refresh remains recoverable under existing semantics.
The authenticated approval page shows code and client identity, requires explicit action and handles success, denial, expiry and API failure without exposing device_code.

stopConditions: Any implementation requires a database schema or migration.
Any credential would be placed in a URL, browser storage, log or response other than the one-time desktop exchange/refresh body.
A read or tool-key capability cannot be mapped to an existing authenticated API owner.
V1 compatibility changes or the approval flow can create more than one session per device code.
Deployment or production configuration becomes necessary.
